newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher for all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher for all months.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher across the board on Thursday, reflecting the stronger Chicago corn market and the yen's weaker tone against the dollar.
Prices were 70 to 400 yen higher, with the benchmark September 1997 contract up 70 yen at 16,130 yen per tonne. Volume was 55,458 lots.

Active buying orders emerged from individual investors from the opening, and some months rose by almost the daily 500 yen limit. Some saw technical selling later as the market lost buying momentum, the traders said. "Investors are quick to sell after price gains," a brokerage trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $3.11-1/2 per bushel at 0820 GMT, against $3.12-1/4 at Wednesday's close.
Spot November of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.94 at 0825 GMT, against $7.95-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
